title: cuda-oxide pure-Rust RoPE (adjacent-pair) port — GB10 sm_121 A/B vs hand-PTX

target_kernel.name: rope
target_kernel.class: f32 FMA + sin/cos/ex2 transcendental (ZERO DP4A) = GO class
target_kernel.launch: grid = num_heads blocks, block = head_dim/2 threads, one rotation pair per thread
target_kernel.why_candidate: RoPE apply is decode-hot (Q and K, every layer, every token), pure trig+FMA, NOT DP4A/INT8-bound, and not yet ported (attention/RMSNorm/SwiGLU already GO; only Q4K GEMV/FFN stay hand-PTX)

baselines.loaded_via: ctx.load_module_from_ptx_src + cuda_core::launch_kernel_on_stream (true on-device A/B, same data + grid + GPU-event timing)

perf.method: FAIR matched single-launch A/B; grid=num_heads x block=head_dim/2 BOTH sides, one launch each; GPU-event median of 5x100; no launch-count confound
perf.run_to_run: best ratio swings 0.984x-1.116x over 4 runs, centered ~1.00-1.05x = statistical tie at the DRAM-bandwidth roofline (~2us both sides)
perf.interpretation: adjacent-pair RoPE is DRAM-bandwidth-bound (1 load + 1 store per element); neither hand-PTX nor oxide can beat the memory wall, both sit at roofline; the GO is a TIE, not a speedup

conclusion: GO — pure-Rust cuda-oxide RoPE is bit-parity-correct (cos=1.0) and matches hand-PTX RopeKernel at every decode shape (incl. Qwen2.5 theta=1M) with NO hand-PTX and NO GH-480 Blackwell-JIT workaround. Confirms the rule: FMA/softmax/transcendental kernels = GO class (alongside PMAT-882/893/894); only DP4A-bound Q4K GEMV/FFN (PMAT-881) is NO-GO. Production migration is a follow-up.
